mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the rank IC falls below 0.05 in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a significant contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when unemployment is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 6% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market that boosts wage pressures and inflation, prompting the Fed to raise rates and depressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation is simultaneously falling.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for four consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12M MA by > 3% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong consumer spending growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in UNRATE above 5% and a fall in PAYEMS below its 6-month moving average by more than 1% over two months signals labor market imbalances that increase recession risk, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% AND PAYEMS < 6M MA by > 1% for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when GDP growth is accelerating.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in HOUST below its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals weakening housing demand, which reduces construction-related earnings and drags on S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12M MA by > 10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rising mortgage rates.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in FEDFUNDS of more than 0.75 percentage points signals an aggressive tightening stance that immediately raises risk-free rates and equity discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when market volatility spikes concurrently.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in GDPC1 above 4% YoY and a fall in CPIAUCSL below 2% YoY for two consecutive months signals a rare combination of strong demand and low inflation, which supports risk assets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 4% YoY AND CPIAUCSL < 2% YoY for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when labor market indicators deteriorate.
